closed: Direct protected-field keyword arguments, nested returned fields and container embedding now traversed recursively.
Existing direct nested getter mutator checks remain independent of alias introduction.
Excluding old RHS field reads addresses the stated self.dtype=getattr(torch,self.dtype) collision in a single ordinary assignment.

findings.source:
self.member = getattr(torch, requested)
alias = self.member
sink(value=alias)  # alternatively return [alias]
findings.reason: Transitive aliases retains alias, but field_aliases drops every one-part path, losing field-origin protection. Recursive escape checks use field_aliases. Preserve protected lineage through direct aliases without changing the separately allowed direct-local-getter boundary.

findings.source: self.member = self.member.ReLU = getattr(torch, requested)  # requested is nn
findings.reason: Python assigns targets left-to-right. First target binds the reflected torch.nn namespace; second writes its ReLU attribute. All origin accesses including targets are currently skipped, not just RHS reads of the previous field value. Refuse/account for overlapping chained targets or restrict old-value exclusion to appropriate RHS reads.

evidence_limits: Both are source-derived falsifiers, not runtime results. No tests/models/output blessing. Earlier A3/S1/A4/P1 and separate ConfigResolution acceptance unchanged. Subsequent corrections require separate review.
